cohorts.subjects: Living adult Saudi patients whose CT of the abdomen or lumbar spine was done in 2015 to 2020 for suspected abdominal pathology or low back ache at one tertiary care centre in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, reviewed retrospectively and taken by consecutive sampling; inclusion age 18 to 60 years; excluded: congenital or acquired deformities, fractures, spondylolysis or spondylolisthesis, and any previous spine surgery, instrumented or not. Ethnicity printed only as Saudi; the authors call the centre representative of the Saudi population and say it serves patients from almost all of the country.
cohorts.n_units: 1,500 lumbar vertebrae (L1 to L5) of 300 patients; left and right pedicles measured (Inference: 3,000 pedicles)

techniques.instrument: Noncontrast CT from L1 to the fifth sacral vertebra in 2.5 mm contiguous axial sections (140 kV, 500 mA, 0.7 s rotation, 200 images, 5 s total exposure, DLP 700 to 900 mGycm), read on a GE AW 5 workstation with GE Centricity Enterprise zero footprint software 6.0 SP4; the measuring tool is not named
techniques.how: On axial sections, after Vaccaro and Garfin: transverse pedicle diameter is the medial to lateral outer cortical width at the isthmus; chord length runs along the pedicle mid-axis from the posterior cortical entry point to the anterior vertebral cortex; pedicle length runs along the mid-axis from the posterior pedicle cortex to the posterior longitudinal ligament; the pedicle axis angle lies between the mid-axis and the midline. L1 to L5, left and right.
techniques.magnification: not applicable: distances and angles read on CT images at a workstation; calibration not described
techniques.observers: two radiologists of equal experience, each measuring every parameter three times, the average taken; inter-rater analysis found no interobserver bias (P > 0.05), statistic not named

techniques.instrument: the same CT series and GE AW 5 workstation; Figure 3B shows a sagittal CT image
techniques.how: Pedicle height is the distance between the superior and inferior pedicle cortex in the sagittal plane at the isthmus, L1 to L5, left and right. Inference: a sagittal reformat of the 2.5 mm axial series, so this measure lies across the slice direction.
techniques.magnification: not applicable: CT image distance; calibration not described
techniques.observers: the same two radiologists, three repeats each, averaged

techniques.how: Means and SDs as each study published them, chosen as CT-based studies that presented adequate data; case reports, plain radiograph measurements, manual measurements on anatomical specimens, intraoperative measurements and studies of children were excluded. Each study's own landmarks, planes and observers are not described here. Inference from the list's own readings: Olsewski's rows are means of cadaver caliper and radiograph columns and Zindrick's pool specimen films with CT, so not every quoted series is CT, and Olsewski's are not values that study printed as such.
Figures the Discussion quotes, cited or not, from work whose methods this paper does not describe; thresholds and recommendations, not measurements of subjects.

within_paper: All of this paper's own values (Tables 1 and 2, the Current study rows of Table 3, Figure 4's Current study line and the text) are the same 300 patients' CT scans measured by the same two radiologists: Table 2 is Table 1 with the sides combined (how is not stated) and Table 3's Current study rows repeat Table 2 (p. 314 (PDF 3); pp. 315-317 (PDF 4-6)). The quoted comparison series are other studies' subjects and share none with this paper. Inference: the Makino Takahiro and Takahiro rows of Table 3 are one study, ref. 24.
